questions.question_text: What is sprint planning in Agile?

options.option_text: A meeting to plan the work for the upcoming sprint
A meeting to review the sprint
A meeting to reflect on the sprint
A meeting to plan the next release

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of sprint planning?

options.option_text: To define what can be delivered in the sprint and how
To plan the next product release

questions.question_text: Who participates in sprint planning?

options.option_text: The Scrum Team: Product Owner, Scrum Master, and Developers

questions.question_text: What is a sprint goal?

options.option_text: A short statement of what the sprint aims to achieve
A list of all team tasks

questions.question_text: What is a sprint backlog?

options.option_text: A list of user stories selected for the sprint
A list of all backlog items
A list of bugs to fix

questions.question_text: What is a sprint retrospective?

options.option_text: A meeting where the team reflects on the sprint
A meeting to plan the next sprint
A meeting to review the product
A meeting to plan the release

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of a retrospective?

options.option_text: To improve team processes and performance

questions.question_text: Who participates in a retrospective?

options.option_text: The Scrum Team: Product Owner, Scrum Master, and Developers

questions.question_text: What is the outcome of a retrospective?

options.option_text: Actionable improvements for the next sprint
A list of completed user stories
A list of bugs to fix

questions.question_text: What is the "Start, Stop, Continue" framework?

options.option_text: A framework where the team identifies what to start, stop, and continue
A framework for reviewing the product

questions.question_text: What is velocity in Scrum?

options.option_text: The amount of work a team can complete in a sprint

questions.question_text: How is velocity calculated?

options.option_text: By summing the story points of completed user stories
By counting the number of tasks completed

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of velocity?
What is a velocity chart?

options.option_text: A chart showing the team's velocity over time

questions.question_text: What is the difference between velocity and capacity?

options.option_text: Velocity measures work completed; capacity measures available team resources

questions.question_text: What is a user story in Agile?

options.option_text: A description of a feature from an end-user perspective

questions.question_text: What is the format of a user story?

options.option_text: As a [role], I want [action] so that [benefit]

questions.question_text: What is a persona in Agile?

options.option_text: A fictional representation of a target user

questions.question_text: What is the difference between a user story and a task?

options.option_text: A user story describes what to build; a task describes how to build it
A task describes what to build
A user story describes how to build it

questions.question_text: What is the "INVEST" criteria for user stories?

options.option_text: Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable
Important, Necessary, Valid, Essential, Specific, Timely
Integrated, Notable, Viable, Efficient, Simple, Tangible
Iterative, Non-negotiable, Valid, Estimable, Specific, Testable

questions.question_text: What is Kanban?

options.option_text: A visual system for managing work

questions.question_text: What is a Kanban board?

options.option_text: A board with columns representing workflow stages

questions.question_text: What are Kanban columns?

options.option_text: Columns like To Do, In Progress, and Done

questions.question_text: What is Work In Progress (WIP) in Kanban?

options.option_text: A limit on how many items can be in progress at once

questions.question_text: What is the difference between Kanban and Scrum?

options.option_text: Kanban is continuous flow; Scrum is time-boxed iterations

questions.question_text: How do you conduct sprint planning?

options.option_text: By selecting backlog items and creating a sprint goal

questions.question_text: How do you estimate user stories in sprint planning?

options.option_text: By using story points or hours to estimate effort
By using a random number generator

questions.question_text: What is capacity planning in sprint planning?

options.option_text: Planning based on team availability and capacity

questions.question_text: How do you prioritize backlog items for a sprint?

options.option_text: By prioritizing based on value, urgency, and dependencies

questions.question_text: What is a sprint planning meeting agenda?

options.option_text: Review backlog, set sprint goal, select items, create sprint backlog
Plan release, create roadmap, set budget
Review sprint, hold retrospective, update backlog

questions.question_text: How do you conduct a retrospective?

options.option_text: By facilitating a structured discussion about what went well and what can improve

questions.question_text: What are common retrospective formats?
What is the "Mad, Sad, Glad" retrospective?

options.option_text: A retrospective where team members share what made them mad, sad, or glad

questions.question_text: What is the "Sailboat" retrospective?

options.option_text: A retrospective where the team identifies risks, anchors, wind, and sun

questions.question_text: How do you turn retrospective feedback into action?

options.option_text: By creating action items and assigning owners

questions.question_text: How do you use velocity for sprint planning?

options.option_text: By using historical velocity to forecast capacity

questions.question_text: What factors affect velocity?

options.option_text: Team size, skill level, and external disruptions

questions.question_text: How do you track velocity over time?

options.option_text: By maintaining a velocity chart over time

questions.question_text: What is the difference between ideal velocity and actual velocity?

options.option_text: Ideal velocity is the target; actual velocity is the real measurement
Ideal velocity is the real measurement

questions.question_text: How do you improve velocity?

options.option_text: By removing bottlenecks and improving team efficiency

questions.question_text: How do you write a good user story?

options.option_text: By following the INVEST criteria and using clear language
By making them as long as possible

questions.question_text: How do you split large user stories?

options.option_text: By breaking them into smaller, independent stories
By combining them into one large story

questions.question_text: What is a story map in Agile?

options.option_text: A visual representation of user activities and stories

questions.question_text: What is the difference between a user story and an epic?

options.option_text: An epic is a large user story that can be broken down into smaller stories
A user story is larger than an epic

questions.question_text: What are acceptance criteria?

options.option_text: Conditions that must be met for a user story to be complete

questions.question_text: How do you implement Kanban?

options.option_text: By setting up a Kanban board and defining workflow stages

questions.question_text: What is a cumulative flow diagram?

options.option_text: A chart showing the flow of work over time

questions.question_text: How do you set WIP limits?

options.option_text: By analyzing team capacity and workflow constraints

questions.question_text: What is a lead time in Kanban?

options.option_text: The time from request to delivery
The time spent on a single task

questions.question_text: What is a cycle time in Kanban?

options.option_text: The time from start to completion of a work item
The time from request to delivery

questions.question_text: How do you handle scope changes during a sprint?

options.option_text: By assessing impact and managing change requests carefully

questions.question_text: What is the difference between sprint planning and release planning?

options.option_text: Sprint planning is for short-term sprint goals; release planning is for larger releases

questions.question_text: How do you estimate large and complex user stories?

options.option_text: By breaking them down into smaller, manageable stories
By estimating them as one large item
By assigning them to someone else

questions.question_text: What is the role of the product owner in sprint planning?

options.option_text: To ensure the sprint backlog aligns with product vision and stakeholder needs

questions.question_text: How do you manage sprint planning in distributed teams?

options.option_text: By using collaboration tools and clear communication

questions.question_text: How do you keep retrospectives engaging?

options.option_text: By using different formats and activities to keep the team engaged
By using the same format every time

questions.question_text: What are anti-patterns in retrospectives?

options.option_text: Blaming, not taking action, and holding ineffective meetings

questions.question_text: How do you measure retrospective effectiveness?

options.option_text: By tracking action items and their outcomes

questions.question_text: What is the "Five Whys" technique in retrospectives?

options.option_text: A technique to find root causes by asking "why" five times

questions.question_text: How do you follow up on retrospective action items?

options.option_text: By reviewing action items in the next retrospective

questions.question_text: How do you normalize velocity across teams?

options.option_text: By using consistent estimation and story point definitions
By using different estimation methods for each team

questions.question_text: What is the difference between velocity and throughput?

options.option_text: Velocity measures work completed; throughput measures work delivered

questions.question_text: How do you use velocity for long-term planning?

options.option_text: By using average velocity to forecast future capacity

questions.question_text: What are the common pitfalls of using velocity?

options.option_text: Comparing velocity across teams and using it as a performance metric
Using velocity to measure individual performance

questions.question_text: How do you communicate velocity to stakeholders?

options.option_text: By explaining velocity as a planning tool, not a performance metric

questions.question_text: How do you write user stories for non-functional requirements?

options.option_text: By describing them as user stories with acceptance criteria
By writing them in technical language

questions.question_text: What is the role of user stories in product discovery?

options.option_text: They help test hypotheses and validate product ideas

questions.question_text: How do you prioritize user stories in a backlog?

options.option_text: By using value-based prioritization methods like MoSCoW or RICE

questions.question_text: What is the difference between a user story and a job story?

options.option_text: User stories are from the user's perspective; job stories describe tasks
Job stories are from the user's perspective

questions.question_text: How do you handle dependencies between user stories?

options.option_text: By mapping dependencies and sequencing work

questions.question_text: How do you implement Kanban for software development?

options.option_text: By setting up a board, defining workflow, and limiting WIP

questions.question_text: What is the difference between Kanban and Scrum?

options.option_text: Kanban is continuous flow; Scrum is time-boxed iterations

questions.question_text: How do you measure Kanban success?

options.option_text: By tracking lead time, cycle time, and throughput

questions.question_text: What is the role of a Kanban board in Agile?

options.option_text: It visualizes work and helps manage flow
It replaces the need for a backlog
It is only for project managers

questions.question_text: How do you combine Kanban with Scrum?

options.option_text: By using Kanban for flow management and Scrum for planning

questions.question_text: How do you scale sprint planning across multiple teams?

options.option_text: By using scaled Agile frameworks like SAFe or LeSS
By having each team plan separately

questions.question_text: What is the difference between sprint planning and PI planning?

options.option_text: Sprint planning is for sprints; PI planning is for Program Increments
Sprint planning is for Program Increments

questions.question_text: How do you handle sprint planning in large-scale Agile frameworks?

options.option_text: By coordinating dependencies and aligning with program goals

questions.question_text: What is the role of sprint planning in product strategy?

options.option_text: It ensures sprint work aligns with overall product strategy
It is only for project managers

questions.question_text: How do you optimize sprint planning for complex projects?

options.option_text: By using data, team input, and continuous improvement

questions.question_text: How do you scale retrospectives across multiple teams?

options.option_text: By holding scaled retrospectives with representatives from each team
By having each team retrospect alone

questions.question_text: What is the difference between team and program retrospectives?

options.option_text: Team retrospectives focus on team-level improvements; program retrospectives focus on cross-team improvements

questions.question_text: How do you measure the ROI of retrospectives?

options.option_text: By tracking action items completed and improvements made

questions.question_text: What are advanced retrospective techniques?

options.option_text: Systems thinking, appreciative inquiry, and futurespective

questions.question_text: How do you build a culture of continuous improvement?

options.option_text: By encouraging open communication and acting on feedback

questions.question_text: How do you use velocity for portfolio planning?

options.option_text: By using velocity to forecast work for multiple teams

questions.question_text: What is the difference between velocity and predictability?

options.option_text: Velocity measures work done; predictability measures consistency

questions.question_text: How do you balance velocity and quality?

options.option_text: By maintaining quality standards and not sacrificing quality for speed

questions.question_text: How do you use velocity for budgeting and forecasting?

options.option_text: By using historical velocity and trend analysis

questions.question_text: What are the limitations of velocity as a metric?

options.option_text: Velocity is a planning metric, not a performance metric

questions.question_text: How do you write user stories for a global product?

options.option_text: By considering cultural differences and diverse user needs

questions.question_text: What is the role of user stories in product-led growth?

options.option_text: They help drive product growth by aligning with user needs

questions.question_text: How do you use user stories for innovation?

options.option_text: By using stories to explore new ideas and gather feedback

questions.question_text: What is the difference between user stories and outcome-based requirements?

options.option_text: User stories focus on user needs; outcome-based requirements focus on business outcomes
Outcome-based requirements focus on user needs
User stories focus on business outcomes

questions.question_text: How do you evolve user stories over the product lifecycle?

options.option_text: By regularly reviewing and updating stories

questions.question_text: How do you implement Kanban at enterprise scale?

options.option_text: By using scaled Kanban practices like portfolio Kanban

questions.question_text: What is the difference between Kanban and Lean?

options.option_text: Lean is a philosophy; Kanban is a method for implementing Lean

questions.question_text: How do you measure Kanban maturity?

options.option_text: By assessing flow efficiency, lead time, and maturity levels

questions.question_text: What is the role of Kanban in DevOps?

options.option_text: It helps manage and improve workflow in DevOps processes

questions.question_text: How do you optimize Kanban for complex workflows?

options.option_text: By continuous improvement and adapting Kanban to workflow needs
